entries.reason: Authored: thatch sheds water only when steep, so a thatched ridge rises as far as it runs (45 degrees), is laid thick, and overhangs its walls deeply to throw water clear of them. Its ridge runs along the building's longer side, as a roof spanning the shorter side does. Each figure is a chosen default, picked by eye from how such roofs are commonly built; none is measured from a source.

entries.reason: Authored: a canvas roof is a tent's: its two sides run from the ridge down to the ground, so the walls beside them are not drawn (they stay in the walk, since nobody walks through canvas), and its ridge runs along the way the door faces, so the door stands in an end. It rises a little more than it runs, which gives standing room along the middle. Each figure is a chosen default, picked by eye from how such roofs are commonly built; none is measured from a source.
